findings.passage: The governor and House Democrats both came out with proposals this week that would burden responsible gun owners while doing little to actually improve public safety. Their proposal to ban commonly owned firearms, add insurance requirements on guns, and create a heap of new regulations will not stop criminals who already ignore the law.
findings.note: In his own legislative update he objects to the governor's and House majority's gun proposals: a ban on commonly owned firearms and gun insurance requirements.

findings.passage: I am a staunch supporter of the Second Amendment and oppose these gun-control proposals, tooth and nail.
findings.note: He states support for the Second Amendment and opposition to the 2026 gun-control proposals; he says to focus instead on repeat offenders, law enforcement and mental health.

findings.passage: As a staunch Second Amendment supporter, I’d like to share some of my concerns over a radical anti-gun bill (S.F. 4067) Senate Democrats passed this week on a 34-33 party-line vote.
findings.note: In his legislative update he voices concerns over S.F. 4067, passed by the Senate 34-33.

findings.passage: There is concern this bill would do more to impact Minnesotans who use their firearms and magazines for self-defense, hunting and sport shooting than shut down violent criminals. This bill clearly is unconstitutional, but the good news is it will go nowhere in the House because Republicans are united in opposition.
findings.note: He says S.F. 4067 (semi-automatic firearm ban, magazine limit over 17 rounds, registration with the BCA renewed every three years, retroactive binary trigger ban) affects lawful owners more than criminals, calls it unconstitutional, and expects it to stall in the House.
